Gap takes SOXX to the top of its two-week range, +8.1% median vs 50d, with the 10Y at a 24-year high; Asia confirmation argues against a full fade. Expect the gap to hold, not build. Diverges from the gap sign on purpose (spec 13)

summary.bottom_line: Hold what you have and don't add chip stocks today. Micron's strong results are already in tonight's pre-market prices, and I expect the main groups to finish close to where they are now unless the 10-year yield breaks higher after the 10pm US factory survey.
summary.where_we_are: 7:13pm SGT (7:13am New York). US pre-market is open and the regular session starts at 9:30pm SGT. Singapore closed at 5pm. Tonight: US weekly jobless claims at 8:30pm SGT (analysts expect 201,000, last week 197,000) and the ISM manufacturing survey at 10pm SGT (analysts expect 54.8, last month 54.6) (Investing.com, 1 Oct). Tomorrow: the US September jobs figures come at 8:30pm SGT, after both closes this read covers.
summary.macro_attribution: The 10-year Treasury yield has moved most: 5.29% at Wednesday's close, up from 5.11% five sessions earlier (prices), and about 5.32% overnight, the highest since 2002 (Reuters via Investing.com, 1 Oct). Oil ($91.7, +1.2%), the dollar (+0.3%) and the VIX (16.3) barely moved. Every lean below depends on that yield.
what_happened: Asia closed strong on Micron's results: Nikkei +3.2%, Korea +2.0%, Taiwan +0.2% (prices). Memory makers led on real trading: SK Hynix +3.1%, Samsung +2.6% (prices; Investing.com, 1 Oct).

Micron itself is down 0.3% before the US open (prices), after dipping about 1% earlier (Reuters via Investing.com, 1 Oct), despite beating forecasts and forecasting next quarter's revenue at about $61.5 billion (CNBC, 30 Sep). The stock has more than tripled this year, so the buying has moved to its peers instead.

Chip stocks are +1.1% before the US open, 17 of 18 names up, led by Tower Semiconductor (a contract chipmaker) +4.4% (prices). Pre-market trades carry no volume, so this is thin until the open confirms it.

Bond selling deepened overnight: the 10-year touched 5.32% and the 30-year 5.66%, after Treasuries' worst quarter since 1994, with Japanese and European bonds also under pressure. Dow futures hit a three-month low early on (Reuters via Investing.com, 1 Oct); Nasdaq futures have since improved to +0.7% and S&P futures to +0.3% (prices).
Singapore slipped: the STI closed -0.2%, OCBC -1.3%, UOB +0.8%, DBS flat, all on about 1.3-1.4x usual volume (prices). I found no bank-specific news.

per_group.semis: Flat. Micron's results are already in the +1.1% pre-market move, and Micron itself being red says the good news is priced. The move takes chip stocks to the top of their two-week range, about 8% above their 50-day average, with yields at a 24-year high. But memory makers rose in Asia on real trading, so I expect the move to hold, not build or fully reverse. Memory makers other than Micron, and Tower, should do best; Micron should lag.
per_group.big_tech: Flat. Alphabet +1.9% leads a +0.6% pre-market move, but these are the stocks most sensitive to the 10-year yield. They held up all week while it rose about 0.18 points, and tonight's figures decide whether it rises further.
per_group.sg_banks: Flat at tomorrow's close, and this one is a coin flip. The banks split today on heavier trading with no news I could find, higher US yields help their lending margins but hurt appetite for stocks, and Friday's session ends before the US jobs figures.
per_group.market: Flat. S&P futures +0.3% are the Nasdaq's gain offset by weakness elsewhere, with Dow futures at a three-month low earlier on the yield jump. I expect the two to roughly cancel. The VIX (the market's fear gauge) is calm at 16.

change_my_mind: If the 10-year yield moves through 5.35% after the 10pm factory survey, chip stocks and big tech give back the pre-market gain (both lower).
If the 10-year falls back under 5.25%, the Micron rally extends and chips close higher.
If Micron turns green in the first hour and the other memory names keep rising, the good news wasn't fully priced (chips higher).
If the Nasdaq's gain fades by 11pm SGT while the Dow keeps falling, the whole market closes lower.
summary.confidence: the one real piece of news, Micron, is already in the pre-market price, and the rest hangs on a bond selloff that kept going yesterday even though US inflation figures came in softer than expected.
summary.cant_know: Whether the global bond selloff keeps running tonight regardless of the figures; it ignored softer inflation yesterday. The 2-year and 30-year yields are not in my price feed, only in headlines.
summary.the_call: Flat, and mild for the market as a whole. Chips move most in either direction, with memory makers other than Micron and Tower leading and Micron itself lagging. The broad market moves least, as the tech gains and the Dow's weakness cancel out.
